content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To tell if jordans are fake, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Check the box label font for inconsistencies (5 minutes)
Step 2. Measure the height of the tongue (2 minutes)
Step 3. Compare the box logo color to a retail pair (10 minutes)
Step 4. Examine the Jumpman logo's stitching (15 minutes)
Step 5. Research the specific release date and colorway (30 minutes)
Step 6. Verify the seller's reputation and history (1 hour)
Step 7. Inspect the box's structural integrity (3 minutes)
Step 8. Smell the shoes for strong chemical odors (1 minute)
Step 9. Check the SKU number on the box against the interior tag (2 minutes)
Step 10. Examine the hourglass shape of the heel from behind (5 minutes)
Step 11. Review high-resolution retail photos online (20 minutes)
Step 12. Cross-reference all findings with a legit-check app (15 minutes)
Step 13. Test the flexibility of the sole (30 seconds)
Step 14. Analyze the texture of the leather panels (10 minutes)
Step 15. Weigh each shoe on a digital scale (2 minutes)
Step 16. Inspect the tissue paper inside the box for the correct pattern (2 minutes)
Step 17. Use a blacklight to look for invisible factory stamps (10 minutes)
Step 18. Check the placement of the "Wings" logo (5 minutes)
Step 19. Evaluate the quality of the paint on the midsole (10 minutes)
Step 20. Count the number of ventilation holes on the toe box (3 minutes)
Step 21. Make a final determination on authenticity (10 minutes)
Step 22. Inspect the stitching on the pull tab (4 minutes)
Step 23. Photograph the shoes from multiple angles (15 minutes)
Step 24. Clean the exterior of the box to see details clearly (5 minutes)
Step 25. Search for common "batch flaws" for this specific model (45 minutes)
Step 26. Check the thickness of the ankle collar padding (3 minutes)
Step 27. Use a magnifying glass to see thread density (12 minutes)
Step 28. Look for the price MSRP tear-away tab on the box (1 minute)
Step 29. Join a sneaker enthusiast forum for second opinions (1 hour)
Step 30. Record all discrepancies in a notebook (10 minutes)
Step 31. Verify the UPC barcode using a scanning app (5 minutes)
Step 32. Open the box and remove all packaging (2 minutes)
Step 33. Press down on the toe box to check the pop-back speed (5 seconds)
Step 34. Download a guide on "Real vs Fake" for this silhouette (10 minutes)
Step 35. Compare the font on the size sticker (5 minutes)
Step 36. Ask for a proof of purchase or receipt (1 day)
Step 37. Check for the presence of a "YDM" sticker inside the box (1 minute)
Step 38. Feel the interior lining material (2 minutes)
Step 39. Examine the stitching under the insole (8 minutes)
Step 40. Measure the width of the shoelaces (1 minute)
Step 41. Inspect the "Nike Air" branding on the tongue tag (6 minutes)
Step 42. Check the transparency of the outsole (4 minutes)
Step 43. Look for the manufacturing date on the size tag (2 minutes)
Step 44. Watch a video comparison of this specific shoe (15 minutes)
Step 45. Check the spacing between the lace holes (4 minutes)
Step 46. Inspect the glue lines along the midsole (7 minutes)
Step 47. Check the orientation of the stars on the toe of the sole (3 minutes)
Step 48. Review the placement of the Swoosh (5 minutes)
Step 49. Check for the correct shade of "University Blue" (5 minutes)
Step 50. Request detailed "tagged" photos from the seller (2 hours)
Step 51. Verify the box dimensions with a tape measure (3 minutes)
Step 52. Analyze the font of the "Made in China" text (4 minutes)
Step 53. Pull out the insoles to check the bottom pattern (2 minutes)
Step 54. Compare the traction pattern on the outsole (5 minutes)
Step 55. Check for the "over-the-shoulder" stitching flaw (5 minutes)
Step 56. Inspect the transparency of the plastic lace tips (2 minutes)
Step 57. Look at the logo on the footbed (3 minutes)
Step 58. Read guides on the specific factory codes (30 minutes)
Step 59. Check the quality of the cardboard used for the box (2 minutes)
Step 60. Check for any "widow's peaks" on the leather cuts (4 minutes)
Step 61. Look for the RFID chip behind the box label (5 minutes)
Step 62. Gather all necessary tools like a flashlight and scale (10 minutes)
Step 63. Check the color of the stitching on the midsole (2 minutes)
Step 64. Zoom in on the pixelation of the box label (8 minutes)
Step 65. Verify the shape of the toe cap (5 minutes)
Step 66. Search for the style code on the official Nike website (10 minutes)
Step 67. Compare the weight of the box to known retail standards (5 minutes)
Step 68. Look for a production stamp inside the shoe (2 minutes)
Step 69. Check the "Registered Trademark" symbol on the tongue (3 minutes)
Step 70. Inspect the corner stitch near the Swoosh (4 minutes)
Step 71. Use a flashlight to check the transparency of the air unit (5 minutes)
Step 72. Examine the laces for the correct weave pattern (5 minutes)
Step 73. Locate a retail reference pair for side-by-side comparison (2 hours)
Step 74. Take the shoes out of the box and place them on a flat surface (1 minute)
Step 75. Measure the distance from the heel to the pull tab (3 minutes)
Step 76. Check the font thickness on the insole (2 minutes)
Step 77. Look for any loose threads on the interior (2 minutes)
Step 78. Compare the heel tab height (4 minutes)
Step 79. Inspect the texture of the shoelace aglets (1 minute)
Step 80. Check for the correct "Nike" logo on the outsole (3 minutes)
Step 81. Inspect the depth of the "Wings" logo embossing (5 minutes)
Step 82. Check the size tag for "bold" font errors (5 minutes)
Step 83. Inspect the stitching on the inside of the tongue (5 minutes)
Step 84. Examine the quality of the box printing (4 minutes)
Step 85. Research the retail price of the shoe at launch (15 minutes)
Step 86. Check the reflective 3M material with a camera flash (2 minutes)
Step 87. Browse professional authentication service blogs (20 minutes)
Step 88. Look for a QR code on the size tag (2 minutes)
Step 89. Summarize all findings of potential flaws (10 minutes)
Step 90. Ask the seller for the original shipping invoice (3 hours)
